newsitem.title: USA: SEC clears MSRB amendments to "pay-to-play" rule.
newsitem.headline: SEC clears MSRB amendments to "pay-to-play" rule.

text.p: The SEC said it approved a Municipal Securities Rulemaking Board proposal to exempt possibly hundreds of securities firms from MSRB's political contributions reporting and recordkeeping requirements.

The revision, to be announced in the Federal Register this week, says if a dealer has no muni finance staff on board then firm executives and management committee members need not report quarterly to the board and keep contributions records.
Previously, MSRB's political contributions Rule G-37 said executives and management committee members had to report contributions even if staff did only occasional muni trades for customers.
But the board said it makes no sense for executives of firms that do no negotiated municipal underwriting to report.
The board warned, however, firms that shift gears and embark on negotiated underwriting will be covered by rule G-37, the board said.
Enacted in April 1994, rule G-37 bars muni dealers that make contributions to issuer clients from doing business for two years with those governments.

In other provisions, the SEC approved amendments make clear that rule G-37 covers governors and other state officials that are not actual bond issuers. Some bond firms argued that the rule was never intended to cover such players.

SEC also approved an MSRB amendment that makes clear that financial advisor work won by dealers on a negotiated basis is covered by G-37. That is the case even if the deals they will be handling are competitive, as opposed to negiatiated, offerings, the MSRB rule says.
SEC also cleared an amendment that requires firms to keep a certified or registered mail record of their quarterly reports filed with MSRB.
